resources.string: Enter what you can do – e.g. a pull-up with +20\u00A0kg for 5\u00A0reps, or a 32\u00A0kg pick-up on 20\u00A0mm for 10\u00A0s with the right hand – or run a short test. CruxCoach turns it into today\'s loads: loaded reps with two in reserve, max hangs at about 90\u00A0%, repeaters at about 65\u00A0% of your 10-second maximum, bodyweight reps and holds at about 70\u00A0% of your maximum. When a logged set shows you are stronger, the value rises by itself and the next session plans more. Your first session with an exercise also sets a first value.
Log your body weight first: added-weight values and % body weight need it.
Paused while the injury is open.
CruxCoach then plans from the value before it, or from your training.
The heaviest set you can do cleanly: load and reps (1–30). From that CruxCoach estimates your one-rep max.
The most you can hold: load, hold time and edge. 10\u00A0s is the reference; other times are converted.
Your maximum number of clean reps in one set.
What you manage in training without failing, e.g. 5\u00A0×\u00A05 at +20\u00A0kg. CruxCoach plans exactly that and finds your limit from your sets.
Hangs you manage cleanly for several sets, e.g. 5\u00A0×\u00A010\u00A0s at +10\u00A0kg on 20\u00A0mm. CruxCoach plans exactly that and learns from every set.
Reps you manage in every one of several sets, e.g. 3\u00A0×\u00A08.
How long you hold in every one of several sets, e.g. 3\u00A0×\u00A045\u00A0s.
